page: Microsoft Azure FX24-12ms_v2 is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, it is allocated 12 vCPUs derived from 6 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The underlying x86_64 architecture features a large 260 MB L3 cache, along with modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptography. It provides 504.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an exceptionally high allocation of 42.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no local storage and does not feature bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2249.0 points (top 10%) and top-tier text processing at 2988.0 points. Compression workloads perform well, achieving 34.73 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 14.22 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In contrast, aggregate multi-core throughput aligns with the moderate 12-vCPU count, posting an average PassMark CPU score of 22851.5 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10862.0. Memory throughput reaches 63.43 GB/sec on large read blocks, but the PassMark memory score falls into the lower 25% percentile despite the large capacity.

With a 1:42 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the FX24-12ms_v2 prioritizes substantial memory density per core over raw parallel thread scaling. This architectural configuration yields strong qualitative cost efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis that requires massive working sets. However, users must account for network or attached remote storage dependencies, as no ephemeral local disks are included. The platform is well suited for memory-bound applications, large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), and cache-intensive workloads requiring high per-thread clock frequencies.
